newsitem.title: PERU: Peru sees 14 new hydrocarbon contracts by end '97.
newsitem.headline: Peru sees 14 new hydrocarbon contracts by end '97.

text.p: The Peruvian government hopes to sign with 14 new oil and gas exploration and production contracts with private oil companies by the end of next year, Energy Minister Alberto Pandolfi said Wednesday.

"In the rest of the year we hope to sign six more contracts, and we estimate for 1997 the signing of eight new contracts," Pandolfi, who is also prime minister, told an oil and gas conference in Lima.
He added that 33 contracts, giving concessions to private companies, were currently in effect - 18 for exploration, and 15 for production.
In addition to the contracts with private oil companies, the government is in the midst of privatizing oil assets currently belonging to state-run Petroperu.

To date this year, sales of company assets include its lubricants unit Petrolube to Mobil for $18.9 million and the La Pampilla refinery by a consortium led by Spain's Repsol for $180.5 million. Block 8/8X was awarded to a consortium led by Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp in June for $142.2 million while U.S.-based independent Anadarko won Block 84 in the jungle block of Ucayali.
